examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Some Unknowns Given the Graph of a Transformed Reciprocal Function
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/fb46d056a8d8010eca509543c231c875f4980a21f1af17505fa98c8c64106207.png)

The diagram above shows the graph of $y = \dfrac{a}{x-b}+k.$ What is the value of $a+b+k?$
examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the horizontal asymptote of the graph is $y=-1,$ while the vertical asymptote is $x=2.$ This means that $k=-1$ and $b=2,$ and we can re-write our function as

$$
y = \dfrac{a}{x-2}+(-1) = \dfrac{a}{x-2}-1.
$$

Also, we are given that the point $(3,2)$ lies on the graph. Substituting its coordinates into the equation above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{a}{x-2}-1 \\ 2 & =\frac{a}{3-2}-1 \\ 3 & =\frac{a}{1} \\ a & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $a+b+k = 3+2+(-1) = 4.$

feedback.problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-\frac{2}{x-2}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To plot $y=-\frac{2}{x-2},$ we apply the following steps:

- Take the curve $y=-\frac{1}{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/9da0db2e6c97e507e82b7ca801e46802fabf91ad31ff53ad3cc9ae580151370a.png)

- Translate it by $2$ units to the right to get the graph of $y=-\frac{1}{x-2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/3c8dd0e4726747b00e4377e43c06693326e10db2977257c9c20da4953127ddfd.png)

- Then, stretch the result by a scale factor of $2$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of $y=-\frac{2}{x-2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13831126/assets/207dec9757b65a75c25ba7ace7a12bec8e922bda9018e58d6511d12de47426b7.png)
